notes.iron1: The beginning of everything. And the man who now plays Doom became an icon here — exactly why the casting hits so hard.
notes.hulk: Ross later becomes President and Red Hulk (Brave New World). Otherwise skippable.
notes.iron2: First appearance of Natasha Romanoff. Not needed for Doomsday.
notes.thor1: Origin of Thor AND Loki, two central Doomsday figures.
notes.cap1: Evans origin; chronologically the starting point, 1943.
notes.av1: The Battle of New York is the pivot of Endgame AND Loki: this is exactly where the variant is born who holds all timelines today.
notes.iron3: Trevor returns in Wonder Man. Otherwise optional.
notes.thor2: Loki's 'death' no. 2; Endgame time-travel destination. Skippable.
notes.cap2: Debut of Sam AND Bucky-as-Winter-Soldier — two Doomsday leads. And the film with which the Russos earned the trust for Endgame & Doomsday.
notes.gotg1: Cosmic MCU foundation; marginal for Doomsday.
notes.av2: Highly relevant again because of Vision Quest: Ultron (James Spader!) and Vision's origin are here.
notes.antman1: The Quantum Realm later becomes Endgame's time machine and Kang's prison.
notes.cw: The foundation: the Avengers break apart. Without this rupture, nothing afterwards makes sense.
notes.strange1: The MCU's magic fundamentals. Doom's second power source beside technology.
notes.spider1: Holland's Peter begins here; his road ends (for now) in Brand New Day.
notes.thor3: Thor's reinvention; Asgard's end explains his current status.
notes.bp1: Wakanda foundation for Shuri, M'Baku and Wakanda Forever.
notes.iw: The Russo blueprint for Doomsday: the villain wins.
notes.antman2: The Quantum Realm accident that makes Endgame possible in the first place.
notes.cm: Carol's origin; basis for The Marvels.
notes.eg: The time-travel mechanic opens the multiverse door — and Tony's farewell is the context that makes RDJ's return as Doom truly hurt.
notes.spider2: The unmasking is the direct trigger of No Way Home. Fun fact: Mysterio's multiverse lie came true two years later.
notes.wv: 9 episodes. Chaos magic and reality rewriting — the basis for MoM, Agatha and Vision Quest.
notes.fws: 6 episodes. Sam's road to the Captain America who leads the heroes in Doomsday.
notes.l1: THE foundational series of the saga: TVA, timelines, Kang. Without it you only half understand Doomsday.
notes.bw: Half the Thunderbolts family starts here. Direct pipeline to the New Avengers.
notes.wi: Multiverse feeling in its purest form; Captain Carter and Infinity Ultron as a foretaste of variant chaos.
notes.sc: Simu Liu is in the Doomsday cast; the rings signal is still open.
notes.et: The dead Celestial becomes the adamantium source of Brave New World.
notes.hk: 6 episodes. Kate Bishop — Young Avengers building block.
notes.nwh: The multiverse breaks into cinema in a big way for the first time — Fox and Sony worlds are officially real.
notes.mk: 6 episodes. Strong, but (so far) without saga connection.
notes.mom: Introduces incursions — the mechanism behind Doomsday and Secret Wars. Plus: worlds where X-Men and F4 have long existed.
notes.msm: 6 episodes. The MCU's very first mutant mention. Post-credits leads into The Marvels.
notes.tlt: Thor's status quo before his Doomsday return.
notes.shk: 9 episodes. Meta multiverse including the K.E.V.I.N. AI.
notes.bpwf: Shuri, M'Baku, Namor and Namora are all in the Doomsday cast.
notes.qm: The saga plan Doom inherits — and the Council of Kangs is an open thread to this day. Cassie Lang starts here.
notes.g3: Trilogy closer; no direct threads for Doomsday.
notes.l2: Probably the single most important setup for Doomsday, period. Loki's timeline throne is the most obvious target for Doom.
notes.mv: The post-credit scene is the X-Men door opener: Monica wakes up in a foreign universe next to Beast (Kelsey Grammer, Doomsday cast).
notes.ec: 5 episodes. Bridge to Daredevil: Born Again.
notes.x97: Its own (animated) universe, but THE love letter to exactly the X-Men era Doomsday brings back.
notes.dw: Anchor beings, the Void, the Fox multiverse, Gambit's debut — the bridge the old X-Men walk across into the MCU.
notes.ag: 9 episodes. Wiccan is the Young Avengers keystone — and Wanda's legacy lives on.
notes.dba: 9 episodes. The state of the streets before Doomsday.
notes.bnw: Sam as sitting Captain America, adamantium in play, no standing Avengers team: the vulnerable world Doom finds.
notes.tb: Doomsday's active hero team forms — and with Sentry the MCU has, for the first time, a hero-side being on Doom's level. Unstable, though.
notes.ih: 6 episodes. Mephisto's MCU debut, right before the multiverse finale — no coincidence. Phase 5 closer.
notes.f4: The direct lead-in: the post-credit scene is practically the first scene of Doomsday. Phase 6 opener.
notes.eow: 4 episodes of animation. Skippable for Doomsday.
notes.bnd: In theaters since 07/31/2026 — the last theatrical film before Doomsday.
notes.vq: From October 14, 2026 on Disney+ (8 episodes) — the last series before Doomsday; Vision's return could matter in the Avengers conflict.
notes.doomsday: The destination of this timeline. Theatrical release: 12/18/2026 (Germany likely 12/16).
notes.secretwars: Theatrical release: 12/17/2027. As soon as the focus shifts, this hub will be expanded for it.

iron1: Iron Man's debut — the cave origin comes almost 1:1 from here (only Vietnam became Afghanistan).
hulk: Lee/Kirby's origin — modernized in the film from gamma bomb to lab accident.
thor1: The film's grounded small-town tone comes from this run — Straczynski even has a cameo.
cap1: Cap punches Hitler on the cover — older than the US entry into the war.
av1: Loki as the first enemy — as in the film.
Modern look, Fury in the Samuel L. Jackson design (with his permission — years before the casting!).
iron3: Warren Ellis' tech-virus story is the film's skeleton.
cap2: Ed Brubaker's run — the Bucky return that was considered unfilmable.
gotg1: This modern team lineup (not the 1969 one) is the template.
av2: Ultron's comic origin (there it's Hank Pym who creates him, not Tony).
antman1: Scott Lang's debut as the thief who steals the suit — the film's premise.
cw: Mark Millar's event — registration was slimmed down into the Sokovia Accords.
strange1: Ditko's psychedelic dimensions shape the look to this day.
The film's tone and medical ethics.
spider1: The origin — deliberately skipped in the film.
Bendis' teenage tone is the real Homecoming DNA.
thor3: Gladiator Hulk on Sakaar — half the film.
The twilight of the gods from the classic Thor issues.
bp1: Dora Milaje, political-thriller tone, Everett Ross.
iw: Starlin's event: the Snap, half the universe, everything.
eg: The second half of the event — plus Marvel's own time-travel logic.
cm: Carol's modern definition incl. 'Higher, Further, Faster'.
wv: Suburban idyll as horror — the series' DNA.
fws: Isaiah Bradley's story — adopted almost unchanged.
l1: Debut of the TVA (by Walt Simonson).
nwh: The forgetting deal — in the film without Mephisto, with Strange.
msm: Kamala's celebrated origin — fandom, family, Jersey City.
tlt: Jason Aaron's Gorr — considerably more terrifying in the comic.
Jane Foster as Thor, including the cancer dilemma.
shk: Jen breaks the fourth wall — long before Deadpool.
wbn: Moon Knight's debut, by the way — the special only takes the monster tone.
tb: Villains as fake heroes — one of the best twists in comic history.
Jenkins' Sentry incl. the Void concept.
f4: The beginning of the Marvel universe.
Galactus, Silver Surfer, the price of salvation.
doomsday: Incursions, Battleworld, God Emperor Doom — the presumed blueprint.
secretwars: The multiverse dies, Doom rules the remains.
xmen1: The moral template of the early films.
x3: Claremont/Byrne's milestone — barely scratched by the film.
dofp: Two issues (!) that founded an entire subgenre.
logan: Millar's end-times western — the film swaps villains, keeps the soul.
dp1: The humor tone incl. fourth wall.
firstclass: Only the name — the 60s origin is a film invention.
raimi2: Peter quits — including the legendary trash-can image, restaged in the film.
venom1: Venom as an antihero in San Francisco — the film's setting and tone.
sv1: The multiverse of the spider people.
dd1: Fisk dismantles Matt's life — season 3 AND the new series carry the name.
jj: Bendis' noir series — Kilgrave, trauma, all from here.
pun: Ennis' tone between brutality and black humor.
hulk03: Plus Ang Lee's own father psychoanalysis.
howard: Steve Gerber's satire duck — the film didn't get the joke.
blade1: Blade's debut as a side character — the film made him an icon.
dw: Plus two decades of meta references to everything.
ag: Wiccan's road to the Young Avengers (Heinberg/Cheung).
x97: The series adapts 'Lifedeath' and the Genosha material, among others.
